headline: Senator Bernie Sanders has demanded a pause on advanced AI and a permanent ban on superintelligence after OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said society may have to accept some severe cyber incidents from openly released AI models.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 1: Sanders' post is dated Monday 12 Oct, before the 13 Oct window, and the bill itself dates from 23 Sep.
importance_line: The demand matters to the public, to Congress and to AI developers, but it is a post on X backing a bill that has not become law, and Altman's words are known only as Sanders and the outlets quote them.
summary: Newsmax reports that Senator Bernie Sanders, the independent from Vermont, wrote on X on Monday 12 Oct "We must PAUSE advanced AI and permanently BAN artificial superintelligence before it is too late", answering Sam Altman, chief executive of OpenAI, who said on Politico's "Decoded" podcast last week that society would have to accept "some fairly severe cyber incidents" from openly released AI models (ones anyone can download and run) in exchange for the freedom they bring. Newsmax adds that Sanders and Representative Greg Casar, a Texas Democrat, introduced a Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act on 23 Sep that would create a Cabinet-level Department of Artificial Intelligence and set prison terms of up to 20 years, and International Business Times, Singapore edition, notes the bill has not become law.
notes: Newsmax page blocked (HTTP 000); Newsmax's text read on its Yahoo copy (https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/bernie-sanders-urges-permanent-superintelligence-114301410.html) and cross-checked with International Business Times Singapore. Url kept as the Newsmax original.
